question: Does a small (100-300 frame) diverse target-domain failure set, added to the Stage-13 normal augmentation, restore failure sensitivity while retaining the normal-FP improvement?
answer: Partially refuted: failure detection was restored (best of all checkpoints), but the normal-FP improvement was completely lost on held-out sources (FPR 1.000), so the two required properties did not co-exist. Stop experimentation.

skz_heldout.note: All three models evaluated on the canonical skz_eval subset (31 images, 16 groups). Duration-only continuity reference; not a tuning target.

classification.exp4: experimental (failure detection restored but normal FPR regressed to 1.000 on holdout)

root_cause: Count-based balance is not a valid proxy: 100 sub-second near-duplicate failure frames (2 cameras) vs 333 30-35s-spaced normals (7 cameras); effective diversity moves the boundary, not count.
Extreme domain scarcity vs 11.3k frozen frames: adding 100 failures flips the entire boundary; no stable operating point.
The two tails are anti-correlated at threshold 0.5; a single checkpoint satisfies neither simultaneously.
Catastrophic held-out FPR 1.000 indicates overfitting to two failure cameras' visual style, not generalizable failure evidence.
